The 2027 MegaLounge 540 Squeezes a Mega Lounge Inside the Tiniest Campervan
15 photos
Photo: YouTube/The Motorhome Review Channel
Tiny is what tiny does, but never underestimate what creative design, plenty of skill, and a willingness to go against the trend can do in terms of turning even the smallest campervan into a nice two-person RV you won't hate yourself for choosing. Case in point, the MegaMobil Lounge 540.
The MegaMobil Lounge 540, or the MegaLounge 540 as it's also been called, has been around for several years now, changing ever so little from one iteration to the other. That's the surest sign that Slovenian manufacturer MegaMobil hit the right spot from the start with the model.
The only thing the 2027 model year brings new is a series of additional extras. This is the smallest version of the MegaLounge compact RV that MegaMobil offers but it's just as customizable as its bigger siblings. In between the interior and exterior options and the extra packs available, you get the chance to turn your compact RV into a personalized one. It will still be small, but it will be truly yours.
The MegaLounge sits on a Stellantis chassis, whether a Peugeot Boxer or a Fiat Ducato, offered standard with a 140-hp engine and manual transmission, and a 3,500-kg (7,716-lb) maximum permissible weight.
Photo: MegaMobil Both these can be upgraded if you want to, so you can move to automatic and 180 hp, or uprate the maximum weight, in which case you do get more payload capacity but you will also need to upgrade your B Category driving license.
Whatever your choice, one thing won't change: this is one of the tiniest yet most complete campervans on the market right now. The MegaLounge 540 comes in at just 5.4 meters (17.7 feet) of total length and a width of 2.05 meters (6.07 feet), which makes it ideal for driving even in crowded or narrow city streets.
Despite its very compact dimensions, it offers sleeping for as many as four people (though it would hardly be a pleasurable experience), a full wet bathroom, a nice galley, and the Mega Lounge promised in the name itself.
Photo: MegaMobil It also comes with plenty of style and functionality , and nice touches like padded walls, soft-touch ceilings, soft-close cabinetry, and accent lighting. Another noteworthy aspect is how MegaMobil goes the extra length to build storage wherever possible. If you think about it, with an RV this compact, you'd be a fool not to make the most of every inch of space – and MegaMobil are definitely not fools.
The layout puts the bathroom behind the driver's seat, the kitchen on the campside, and that oversize, very comfortable lounge at the back, with an automatic drop-down bed on top. Everything onboard is compact, obviously, except for the lounge, which is perfect for cozy two-person meals and might even work for four.
To that end, MegaMobil builds it with nice backrests with integrated storage and an adjustable table. Another surprise here is that you can also drop the table all the way and convert the entire space into a double bed. Keeping in mind the dimensions of the campervan, sleeping four people in here is a case of "just because you can doesn't mean you should," so keep that as an emergency option.
Photo: MegaMobil The main bed, however, is overhead. It drops down at the press of a button, revealing access to overhead storage and a nice skylight.
The galley is standard, with a two-burner gas cooktop and sink combo, overhead storage, and additional cabinetry under the counter, which also includes a small extension for more prep space. In a bid to add even more functionality, MegaMobil adds another extension to the outside, as well as access to the cabinets from there.
The bathroom is another neat surprise, small as it might be.
Photo: MegaMobil It's a wet one but it works almost like a dry bathroom because MegaMobil uses a glass door that swings out and covers the space where the sink, cassette toilet, and a cabinet are, while also freeing up the washing space. When you don't need the shower, the same door swings over and covers it.
For an RV of this size, having a full bathroom is an absolute luxury – and MegaMobil delivers it.
In terms of standard equipment, the MegaLounge 540 comes in three trims (Core, Advanced, and Premium), to which you can add from a list of optional packages like Escape, Freedom, and Autonomy. The last one, as its name says, offers solar panels on the roof, a 300Ah battery pack, a 2000W inverter, an awning, and an induction cooktop in lieu of the gas variant.
Photo: MegaMobil Standard across all of them will be gas-electric Truma blown air heating, a Truma water heater, a backup camera, tinted flush-mounted windows, a MaxxAir vent fan, A TV on a bracket in the lounge, and 75 liters (20 gallons) of freshwater and 80 liters (21 gallons) of gray. Like most European RVs, regardless of size, the MegaLounge 540 comes with a cassette toilet, which means there is no black water tank onboard.
Sale prices will depend on trim, optional packages , optional colors and fabrics, and lastly, the dealer you source your unit from.
Photo: MegaMobil That said, the price for the 2027 model year starts at €72,173, which is approximately $78,500 at the current exchange rate. It's not the cheapest micro-RV out there, so you could say pricing is the only part about it that's not teeny-tiny.
Via // The Motorhome Review Channel on YouTube

1993 Aston Martin Virage Vacances Was Born a Coupe, It Turned Into a Seven-Seat Shooting Brake
9 photos
Photo: Rm Sotheby's/Corey Escobar
As the world was getting ready to step into a new decade at the end of the 1980s, one that would be characterized by unprecedented change, British carmaker Aston Martin let loose the Virage family of luxury grand tourers.
It was to be a relatively unsuccessful one, having been made from 1989 to 2000, and then briefly revived at the start of the 2010s, but, this being Aston Martin and all, that doesn't necessarily translate into high production numbers.
In fact, very low production numbers would better describe the breed: only 512 of them were made in coupe form, and some 296 in volante, convertible body style. With the exception of the one-off Virage Shooting Brake Zagato Centennial released in 2014, Aston Martin never officially mass-produced this body style for the Virage .
Yet here is one right now, fighting for the attention of the bidders that'll be on location in Phoenix, Arizona, at the end of January 2027, for the sale at the hands of auction house RM Sotheby's of the 59-vehicle Boeckmann Collection.
Part of the batch of 59 cars, the so-called Aston Martin Virage Vacances was originally born in 1993 as a right-hand-drive coupe, but, as soon as it was delivered to its original owner, it was sent back to the carmaker's Works Service shops to be transformed into a Shooting Brake.
Photo: Rm Sotheby's/Corey Escobar That it did, but not before being stripped down to its metal shell so that a 12-inch (30 cm) wheelbase extension could be performed and its steering column moved to the left-hand side.
The makeover was accompanied by an engine swap that had the factory-fitted 5.3-liter V8 taken out and replaced by a larger, 6.3-liter V8 controlled via a dog-leg five-speed manual transmission.
The car's original engine, engineered with help from Callaway Cars, a crew famous for their work with twin-turbocharged Corvettes , was not something one could easily ignore, as it cranked out 335 horsepower. The larger one, of course, had to be more powerful for the swap to make sense, and that's exactly what it delivered, being rated at 475 horsepower.
Naturally, the increase in engine size and power meant that other upgrades had to be made as well. To make sure everything works as intended, the Brits upgraded the suspension system and the braking hardware that was tasked with bringing the Virage to a safe stop.
Photo: Rm Sotheby's/Corey Escobar At the end of the modification effort, the car was bestowed with the Vacances name, which is the French word for vacation, in an attempt to show just how family-friendly the vehicle now was - after all, it did have seven seats now, and a tailgate to top everything off...
This particular Shooting Brake example, chassis 50005, was to become the first of seven Aston Martin Works Service shooting brake conversions, with the rest of them, six, having been delivered to a single owner.
As a side note, all other Virage Shooting Brakes in existence carry a wheelbase that was extended by 16 inches (41 cm), making the one we have here the only one ever designed to use the 12-inch extension.
That's something that could increase the sale value of the car significantly. Normally, a standard Virage goes nowadays for up to $200,000, if the car in question is in tip-top condition. The seller of this Shooting Brake variant hopes to fetch a bit more than that, up to $250,000, if the right crowd is in the house.
Photo: Rm Sotheby's/Corey Escobar That's a bit of a gamble, though, as the car is listed for sale with no reserve, as all other vehicles of the Boeckmann Collection. It remains to be seen whether the Hunter Green paint job used on the bodywork (the interior is specced in gray leather) is enough to lure people in.
It might, seeing how it's probably similar to the original Buckinghamshire Green it had when it left the factory floor. And there's one more aspect going in its favor: a relatively low mileage, with the odometer showing 33,235 miles (almost 53,500 km) since it was made in 1993, meaning an average of roughly 1,000 miles (1,600 km) traveled each year.
We will keep an eye on the 1993 Aston Martin Virage Vacances and report back once we learn how much it eventually ends up selling for.
And we'll also keep an eye on the rest of the cars in the Boeckmann Collection, to bring you some other of the impressive vehicles it includes. Just to give you an idea of what that means, we're dealing with an inventory that includes the world's only Galpin GTR1 and the 1932 Ford Edelbrock Special.
There is also an impressive lineup of 14 Porsches from the good-old days, three Barris Kustom projects, and a bunch of other rarities meant to get the blood pumping and the money flowing. Stay tuned as we give them each their own stories.

The Tiny Drop Is the Wackiest Tiny House, Half Teardrop Trailer and Half Shed
41 photos
Photo: G Wheeler Photography for Tend Building
As much as some people like to rail against tiny houses as overpriced sheds on wheels that have no real value in everyday life, reality itself contradicts them. Tiny houses are valid options for temporary or full-time living, while also delivering the goods in sustainability, mobility, and affordability.
To each their own, as the saying goes. Tiny houses have been disputed since their earliest days and their recent boom in popularity (especially paired with increased prices) has done little to make them less so. This build will do nothing in terms of settling the debate, so let's not get into it.
This is a Blast from the Past story , though the past is as recent as 2016. Still, back then, tiny houses and alternative mobile homes were just strengthening their grip on the niche of alternative housing, and that alone would have made The Tiny Drop a notable entry. The fact that all the other options available were more or less actual sheds on wheels did the rest.
The Tiny Drop was inspired by teardrop trailers, in that it aimed for aerodynamics by borrowing the iconic teardrop shape. It still had to be a house, though, so that inspiration was lost once the front end was designed; the end result became something that looked like an oversized or steampunk teardrop that had crashed into a shed. Or the other way around.
Photo: G Wheeler Photography for Tend Building It was the project of Tend Building from Houston, TX, based on an original design . Tend Building built custom tiny houses for a few years before ceasing activity some time after the completion of this one. The two were not related events; in fact, The Tiny Drop went on a national tour and became a little star on its own.
Construction began in February 2015, when the builders took delivery of a custom tandem-axle trailer from a local manufacturer. On it, they built a wooden frame, adding wood panels and aluminum sheeting outside and even on parts of the interior, like the ceiling.
Rigid insulation was used, not necessarily because the builders had any plans initially to move into it but because they imagined a passive house , so resource efficiency was a must. This odd-looking tiny had to be energy efficient regardless of the weather outside, so it had to have a high-performance building envelope.
Photo: G Wheeler Photography for Tend Building Offering a total of just 150 square feet (14 square meters) of living space, The Tiny Drop was tiny even by all tiny house standards, while being much heavier, at 8,000 lbs (3,629 kg). Still, it was imagined with a full residential entry door, residential windows, and a pair of skylights in the lofted bedroom that opened like butterfly wings. There was no clear intent of making ventilation as dramatic as possible, but it was a striking effect nonetheless.
The interior crammed in every creature comfort possible. At the back, you had a full dry bathroom with a shower, a composting toilet, and a sink with vanity in a bump-out – a technique that some tiny house builders today also prefer to add a bit more space inside.
The lofted bedroom spread over the entire bath and half of the remainder living space. It offered little head height and came with a metal work ladder as the sole form of access, but it fit a double bed in there and had those generous skylights to make the space feel cramped. In tiny houses, choosing your battles is the key to winning the war.
Photo: G Wheeler Photography for Tend Building At the front of the trailer was the living room, which was limited to just a sofa with storage built underneath. Then, the central part of the trailer was reserved for the galley kitchen and a breakfast bar that doubled as dining and working space.
Tend Building mentioned "high-end appliances" for the kitchen but photos published of the interior showed none, so my guess is they were brought in afterwards. They most likely included a removable induction counter and a 12V compact fridge that fit under the counter, since there was no other space where you could fit a larger unit.
The Tiny Drop also came with a window-style AC unit and a furnace, as well as solar panels on the roof of an unspecified capacity. The builders repeatedly told the media that the tiny could run off the grid, in what was supposed to be a piece of evidence about the sustainability of the project. To that same end, it also had a water filtration system that made you could live in it without hooking it up to the mains.
Photo: G Wheeler Photography for Tend Building The builders' commitment to "energy efficiency, affordability and ecological sensitivity in design and construction" was also apparent in the way The Tiny Drop had been built with recycled and upcycled materials. Detailed custom work elevated these old materials and gave this very tiny tiny house lots of personality.
When construction began, the plan was to have it completed for the 2015 Houston Car Parade, but things didn't work out.
The Tiny Drop did appear in the parade, but only as a half-completed shell with no interior. Completion would take another year, after which the house went on a tour before finally settling in Vermont, as the builders' new home.
Photo: G Wheeler Photography for Tend Building Tend Building never replicated The Tiny Drop for another customer. Asked about price on this one, they would often say that they did only custom projects , adding that a similar build would cost about $60,000. That's a lot of money for a tiny house of this size today, but it was an even more preposterous amount a decade ago.
Still, The Tiny Drop was a success, if only for showing people an alternative, wacky way of housing .

The Free Bird Camper Van Blends Homey Comfort With Abundant Storage and Adventure-Ready Capability
16 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Freedom Vans
Meet Free Bird, a camper van conversion based on an AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 2500 with a 170" wheelbase. It blends adventure capabilities with home-like luxuries, packing all you need to hit the road in comfort and style.
This mobile home was created by Freedom Vans, a Bellingham, Washington-based company specializing in high-quality, custom and semi-custom van conversions. We've previously covered other of the company's creations here on autoevolution, such as Planned Spontaneity .
Laying eyes on the vehicle's exterior, you can tell that it was designed for adventuring. For starters, the van rides on alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. At the front, the company fitted an off-road-ready bumper complete with a winch and a hitch receiver.
On top of the rig, you'll discover a custom-built rack holding a Carefree awning, a front-facing LED light bar, a 400 W solar array, and a flat-mounted Starlink antenna.
Two cut-outs were made on the roof to accommodate a Velit A/C unit in the front and a Maxxair vent fan in the back. Other notable exterior mods include Freedom Vans running boards and power and water hookups.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Freedom Vans Stepping inside, you'll be surrounded by a warm and welcoming interior. The customer opted for dark grey cabinetry and warm wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring.
The look is complemented by a butcher block countertop, under-cabinet LED light strips, and a variety of black accents, such as the kitchen hardware and the cabinet and drawer handles. However, the most distinctive aesthetic element is the ceiling, finished with planks of many different colors.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you've set up camp and don't need to drive around anymore.
This front seating area continues further back in the form of a dinette setup. It comprises two benches with a decently sized table between them. The bench toward the back has a top that can be lifted to reveal a storage compartment.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Freedom Vans The other bench has a slide-out ottoman – you can use it to rest your legs, and it also offers room for your things in a compartment similar to the one you can find in the rear bench. Moreover, you can use two overhead cabinets and a headliner shelf for extra storage space.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features a dual-burner induction stovetop, a deep black stainless steel sink with a second filtered water faucet, a fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a flip-up table for additional counter space.
An overhead cabinet, a tiny shelf, five drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage. The latter houses a 5-gallon (19-liter) bucket that serves as a greywater tank. Moreover, one of the drawers doubles as a step that helps you climb into bed.
On the opposite side, Freedom Vans devised a floor-to-ceiling unit. It offers a huge closet with hanging space and a mirror on the door's inside, as well as a cabinet underneath that hides a portable toilet.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Freedom Vans Finally, a sleeping arrangement takes up the rear part of the living space. It boasts a queen-size bed arranged north to south, two reading lights, and an overhead cabinet.
Your bulkiest items will best fit in the garage underneath the bed, which is accessible from both inside and outside the van. To make loading and unloading your items easier, the builders fitted a massive pull-out tray attached to heavy-duty slides that can support up to 500 lb. (227 kg).
Two boxes on the garage's sides accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the left – the electrical system's highlights are a 920 Ah lithium battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. Three charging sources are available: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
On plumbing, the van is equipped with a 36-gallon (136-liter) freshwater tank, a 6-gallon (22-liter) electric water heater, and an outdoor shower connection. The company also created a setup that lets you easily blow out the plumbing lines for winterizing.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Freedom Vans The "command center" for the rig's utilities is easily accessible, located above the rear part of the bed. It includes a battery monitor, a thermostat, an inverter controller, and a controller for the Maxxair vent fan above the bed.
All in all, Freedom Vans transformed this Sprinter van into a cozy yet roam-ready home on wheels. Not only does it look amazing, but it offers a comfortable setup with lots of storage and space to relax.
How about pricing? We don't have a quote for the Free Bird, but we know that a long wheelbase conversion can start at $80,000 (€73,088) for a simpler project and can go to $180,000 (€164,450) or even higher, depending on the features and finishes.

Car Hunter Bought an Armored Mercedes-Benz S63 AMG, Drove 1,300 Miles and Listed It for Sale
39 photos
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube
A professional car hunter bought a bulletproof 2012 Mercedes-Benz S63 AMG and drives around in it as if he were the world's most wanted person. The thing is that he just likes collecting rare Mercedes examples. Still, he says, "It's not a bad thing to drive in New York."
They call him The Barn Find King for a reason. Tim Fabrizio tracks down cars that went off the radar ages ago, cars that everyone thinks might have been crushed, and brings their forgotten histories back into the spotlight. That's what he does for a living.
Finished in black over a white interior, his latest purchase, a 2012 Mercedes-Benz S63 AMG (W221) has Level B6 ballistic protection, one of the highest civilian armor ratings available under European ballistic standards, equivalent to U.S. NIJ Level III. This means that it is engineered to stop high-velocity rifle rounds, including 7.62x51 mm NATO and 5.56x45 mm ammunition fired from assault rifles like an AK-47 or M16.
The model also features thick multi-layer laminated ballistic glass and reinforced steel plating across all doors, body panels, fenders, and pillars. The factory panoramic roof was replaced with a solid armored steel panel, and the underbody was upgraded to protect against hand grenades or anti-personnel explosives.
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube On top of the armor plating, the dashboard had to be reupholstered, and the door panels had to be retrimmed. The armoring experts relocated the speakers to make room for the added protection, but other than that, everything remained stock inside the cabin. Even the soft-close doors still close… softly, despite the extra weight.
Fabrizio's sedan also comes with custom grenade blockers installed inside the exhaust pipes, along with a reinforced suspension to be able to support the extra 1,500 to 2,000 pounds (680 to 907 kilograms) of armor.
The car rolled off the production line in Sindelfingen, Germany, and was converted into the fortress on wheels that it is now in San Antonio by Texas Armoring Corporation. The firm built two such models, and the black Benz is one of them. And you can hardly tell the difference between the bulletproof example and a standard one.
The car was by no means a barn find or a long-lost vehicle. Tim Fabrizio found it on Craigslist, listed by " some of the coolest people " he has ever transacted with. He flew to Connecticut, signed the papers, and drove the Benz home.
{fullim10}
The car had roughly 3,700 miles (5,955 kilometers) on the clock when he bought it, and he's driven it to 4,993 miles (8,035 kilometers) since. Then, he just went past 5,000 miles (8,056 kilometers) while filming for Magnacars, with TJ Lamb in the passenger seat.
He has no idea how much it cost when new or how much the previous owner paid for the conversion, but he assumes it should be around $150,000 - $200,000 on top of the original luxury sedan with sports car credentials.
A standard 2012 Mercedes-Benz S63 AMG started at $139,300, or $140,175 with the destination fee included in the United States. Checking option boxes like the Designo interior or the AMG Performance Package that this car has would take the sticker price past $160,000.
Tim Fabrizio laughs off speculation about this car having been built specifically for a cartel boss. He found paperwork and various items, such as a Chinese flag, stored in the trunk, which confirmed the sedan’s diplomatic background.
Photo: Cars and Bids Since he bought it, he drained all the old fluids, replaced the old tires with run-flat ones, and rebuilt the tracks that allow the car to roll even with the tires punctured. He is dealing with a delaminated windshield, but the glass armoring is not affected. It is, after all, a 14-year-old car, converted from new.
It is still fast (it wears the AMG badge, after all), and the suspension compensates for the extra weight. It looks like an S-Class, it feels like an S-Class, and it drives like an S-Class, but drinks up fuel like a military tank. Under the hood sits the 5.5-liter twin-turbocharged M157 V8. With the Performance Package, the V8 pumps out 563 horsepower (571 metric horsepower) and 664 pound-feet (900 Newton meters) of torque.
The setup is perfectly capable of handling the armoring. In factory form, it pushes the unarmored sedan from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.3 seconds and up to an electronically limited 186 mph (300 kph), though the added weight of the ballistic steel and thick glass noticeably slows down this armored example.
Fabrizio is madly in love with the car. However, he is not going to keep it. He has already listed it on Cars and Bids with 5,006 miles on the clock. With three days to go, the highest bid reached $20,250.
Photo: Cars and Bids He likes to drive his cars, and he wouldn’t feel comfortable adding miles to the odometer of such a pristine vehicle. On top of that, he has recently added several iconic vehicles to his garage, he has recently parked several iconic vehicles in his garage.
He owns Tupac Shakur's Hummer H1 , the final car that the late rapper had, Donald Trump's 1995 Lamborghini Diablo VT, and the long-lost-and-found Victoria’s Secret Lamborghini Diablo.

Dealer-Built 1967 Shelby GT350S Surfaces After 50 Years With One Family, Sports Rare Power Option
51 photos
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins
Finding a genuine 1967 Shelby GT350 tucked in a suburban garage is enough to send any Ford enthusiast's pulse past redline, and go like hell to hunt it down. Finding one wearing blue GT350S rocker stripes, packing a Paxton supercharger, and carrying over 50 years of family history is rarer still. But finding one built on the same day as the example already sitting in your garage is as close to impossible as gearheads could come.
Yet classic car hunter Dennis Collins did just that, purchasing a competition-spec fastback from Kenner, Louisiana. Of course any Shelby Mustang of the original series is a showstopper, but one this rare – that’s an event in itself.
To grasp why this car matters, one has to look back at 1967, the pivotal year Shelby American expanded its lineup. Alongside the debut of the big-block 428-cubic-inch GT500 at $4,195, the small-block GT350 soldiered on at $3,995 with its high-revving 289-cubic-inch K-code V8 (in its final season on the market).
Stock output stood at 306 horsepower at 6,000 rpm and 329 lb-ft of torque at 4,200 rpm (310 PS, 446 Nm), paired with a crisp 4-speed manual or optional 3-speed automatic transmission. For buyers unwilling to sacrifice the small-block car's sharper front-end balance for big-block heft, Shelby offered a $549 Paxton centrifugal supercharger.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins That blown GT350S setup lifted gross output to roughly 390 horsepower at 6,000 rpm (395 PS) and pushed top speed past 150 mph. Out of 1,175 GT350s built in 1967 compared to 2,050 GT500s, only 35 received factory-installed Paxton blowers, and just one of those 35 rolled out painted Wimbledon White.
Dennis Collins already owns that lone factory white Paxton car, Shelby number 1477, currently under restoration with 1967 Shelby specialist Jason Billups. The Louisiana fastback him and his team traveled to inspect is Shelby number 1470. Separated by just 7 Shelby numbers and 5 K-code digits, both white coupes were ordered, bucked, serialized, and sent down the assembly line on the exact same day.
The trail to Kenner came through Scott Sidor, a familiar contact from whom Collins had previously purchased a black Pontiac Trans Am. Scott's brother, Kevin Sidor, had actually worked on the Shelby's supercharger for its longtime caretaker, Kent.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Even before factoring in forced induction, Shelby number 1470 is a scarce machine. Out of the 1967 GT350 4-speed run, only 125 cars left the factory painted white. Because this example was ordered without air conditioning or emissions equipment and specified with optional Kelsey-Hayes Magstar wheels, its configuration narrows down to 1 of 31 built.
Collins also knew from pre-purchase research that the car had entered a dealer pool and received a factory rebate. That status meant nobody ordered the coupe as a factory Paxton car, yet its subsequent trail proved even more fascinating. Paperwork revealed the car sat for several months after assembly before being delivered on September 9, 1967, to original buyer Ronald E. Irwin in Plymouth, Michigan.
Its second owner, Joey LaBella, later acquired the fastback when its previous holder faced federal scrutiny over foreign import cars and scrambled to liquidate his inventory. Over 50 years ago, Kent's father stepped in as the third owner, starting a multi-generational run of family stewardship. The Shelby eventually passed to Kent's brother, who spent roughly three years preparing it for the Great American Race from New York to California.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins He added extra batteries, front and rear charging stations, vintage decals, and extra instruments, even registering for the event, before tragically passing away before the car ever reached the starting line.
Following his brother's death, the supercharged coupe virtually vanished from public roads. Kent admitted he drove it to just one cruise night, quickly discovering that a non-tilt Shelby cabin felt cramped for a 265-pound driver accustomed to roomier A-body muscle cars.
Its last real outing was a local car show around four years ago. Still, Kent preserved it thoughtfully, draining the fuel tank through a rear plug and protecting the original FoMoCo radiator with storage solution.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Resting on the garage floor beside the fastback were two mechanical treasures that sealed the car's historical weight: the original blue Paxton supercharger, confirmed to be one of 100 units Shelby took delivery on from a 200-unit order for 1967. Later, a running 1966-dated Paxton was fitted to the car, after the original began hardware making the wrong kind of noises.
Next to the blower lay a weathered Ford Toploader 4-speed gearbox carrying an aluminum RUG-A tag. Second owner Joey LaBella, still alive when Kent contacted him, confirmed he had tracked down and returned that original transmission to Kent's brother, preserving the drivetrain's numbers-matching status pending a rebuild.
Kent was equally candid about track provenance, noting the car showed clear competition wear and safety modifications even though hard documentation of specific race entries never surfaced.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins One glance inside the black vinyl cabin and engine bay proved this GT350S meant business. Collins called it the most heavily instrumented Shelby he had ever seen, counting two boost gauges, two oil pressure dials, two oil temperature gauges, amps, and water temperature. Twin fire extinguishers, a fuel cutoff, racing harness eyelets, an oversized Shelby catalog oil cooler, an under-hood kill switch, and a dual anti-theft alarm reinforced its unmistakable competition pedigree.
Strange parallels also linked car 1470 to Collins's sister car 1477. While 1477 wears a Holman-Moody fiberglass front end, 1470 carries Holman-Moody fiberglass front fenders alongside its original fiberglass hood, deck lid, and quarter-panel date codes. Beneath Ziebart undercoating and an older repaint, the coupe kept its original short-hub wood-rimmed steering wheel, a Philco radio with a dealer-installed power antenna, Kelsey-Hayes 10-spoke alloys, and spare Magnum 500 wheels.
After crawling beneath the front valence and spotting a Cobra scatter shield from the Shelby performance catalog, Collins needed no further convincing. He shook Kent's hand without haggling a penny, gathered thick binders of vintage documentation, and winched the white fastback into the trailer.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Back at his Texas shop, Collins unpacked the paperwork alongside pre-purchase research from Brian Styles of the Shelby Research Group and a Marti report. Inside sat the ultimate smoking gun: an original 1967 Shelby GT350 owner's manual, authenticated by its cover white-out marks and glued-in two-page warranty section. Opening the front page revealed a verified 1960s-era authentic Carroll Shelby signature facing a typed list of day-one dealer installations.
Labeled a 1967 Shelby Cobra GT350S competition coupe, that typed sheet recorded a 595-cfm Holley carburetor, a nodular Super Duty 3.31:1 rear end, a Ford Special Performance speed coil, a Hayes Eliminator competition clutch, the Cobra scatter shield, a Hurst Competition Plus shifter, and the Shelby American-equipped supercharger. Ironically, while Shelby's manual explicitly voided extended powertrain coverage on blown cars, Kent saved the original Paxton warranty and cards.
That paper trail transforms car 1470 from an intriguing survivor into a documented day-one dealer-built competition artifact. Collins already has a proper set of 1967 Kelsey-Hayes Magstar wheels waiting and plans to send the original steering wheel to specialist Keith Craft for restoration, while Brian Styles and Jason Billups help decode the remaining records. Reunited beside its assembly-line twin 1477 for the first time in 59 years, this supercharged 1967 GT350S will run and drive again soon.

1970 Dodge Challenger SE Packs Big-Block Power, Fender Tag Is Missing
15 photos
Photo: Hemmings
In 1970, Chrysler debuted the E-body platform. Plymouth used it for the third-generation Barracuda, while Dodge developed the then-new Challenger on it. The latter was the last Mopar to join the muscle car market, and it was quite popular initially, moving nearly 77,000 units in 1970.
While the Barracuda was available in three versions, Dodge only offered two variants of the Challenger. Customers could opt between the standard model and the performance-oriented R/T. However, Dodge also offered a Special Edition (SE) package that turned the Challenger into a more luxurious vehicle (similar to Plymouth's Gran Coupe model).
The SE bundle included a vinyl top and, more notably, a smaller rear window. The latter was called the "formal" window and had filler panels around it in order to reduce the glass opening. Dodge also added SE medallions on the pillars and extra bright trim on the sides and trunk lid.
Inside the cabin, the SE package added leather and vinyl bucket seats and an overhead console with warning lights or seat belts, low fuel, and door ajar. The woodgrain accents, the smaller-diameter steering wheel, and other details rounded off the cabin's more premium appearance. The package did not nothing performance-wise, as the SE was available with any engine.
The bundle was relatively popular, finding its way on 9,976 examples. That's nearly 13% of the total Challenger production in 1970. The package was ordered on 6,223 standard models and 3,753 R/T vehicles. The Hemi SE is the rarest of the bunch, with just 60 units made, while three other versions have three-digit production figures to brag about. I'm talking about the 440 R/T (875 units), the 440 Six-Pack R/T (296 examples), and the standard inline-six (350 units).
The yellow hardtop you see here is also a standard model equipped with the SE package, but it was born with a V8 engine. Existing records say that it's one of 5,873 units with a V8 and the SE package, but there's no further breakdown for specific powerplants. The VIN says it was born with a 318-cubic-inch (5.2-liter) small-block V8, which is quite common. It also mates with three-speed automatic, which, again, makes for a very common combo.
But I guess it doesn't matter all that much because the Challenger no longer retains the original mill. The 318 was replaced with a 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) big-block V8. The latter was available on the Challenger in 1970, but it's unclear if this replacement engine is period-correct . But for what it's worth, the VIN confirms that it's an SE-spec hardtop.
The engine swap is not this car's biggest issue, though. The Challenger is also missing its fender tag. This means that we cannot confirm any of the options, and whether the yellow paint is factory-correct or not. The hue appears to be FY1 Top Banana, which was indeed a (brand-new) factory option in 1970.
Issues aside, this is a pretty solid classic. The Challenger was restored in 1990 and has only covered 8,000 miles (12,875 km) since. The 383 V8 was also rebuilt that year. The seller says it's "ready to enjoy now," which should mean that the car runs and drives as it should. With the same owner for 40 years, the Mopar is looking for a new home for $27,500 . How's the sticker for a non-matching Challenger with a missing fender tag?

New Hot Wheels Mainline Case Unboxing: Dodge Super Treasure Hunt Is Coming Up
57 photos
Photo: eBay/User CK_salez
A few days ago, I published a Ferrari-themed Hot Wheels unboxing story. Nine of the ten cars were over 20 years old, so the Enzo was the only new model on the list. As I didn’t pre-order one, I thought a good deal paying $16 for it to a dealer I hadn’t worked with before.
It was already cheaper than I what I had paid for the F50 , and I figured I’d never get an opportunity like it again. But yesterday, one of the toy stores I regularly go to just listed it for $11 and the page doesn’t read “Sold Out” yet.
That’s despite several people on our local collector’s group posting about it. Someone pointed out that “people are trying to save up for Christmas”, which is one way of saying that money is tight for most enthusiasts right now.
It’s either that or the store just has a huge stock of these cars, but I doubt that’s the correct explanation. Anyway, the real reason I started writing this story is that I’ve just spotted the first unboxing video for next year’s Mainline Case D.
You’ll also spots some shots of what is likely an Employee Exclusive version of Bryan Zhao’s Hako Type D. This will be so rare that it will make finding or buying a Super Treasure Hunt feel like a walk in the park.
Regular Treasure Hunt Photo: Hot Wheels Malaysia However, we need to talk about Case D’s Regular Treasure Hunt before moving on into STH territory. Just in case you aren’t aware what Cases A, B and C looked like, allow me to remind you. The 2027 TH collection has so far included three original castings: the El Segundo Coupe, the High-Tail Chaser and the GT Hunter.
There was a good chance that the fourth release would be a licensed model, but some also believed that the Tooned Purple Passion could show up instead. The latter looks great in black with the orange flames, but I’m sure that the '72 Chevy LUV won’t spend too much time on the pegs either.
We haven’t seen a Chevy TH since 2024, when Mattel gave us the ‘47 Fleetline, the Custom ‘53 Chevy and the ‘59 Impala. The Chevy Luv is Ryu Asada’s creation from way back in 2016.
Becoming a Treasure Hunt is one of its biggest achievements after the 2020 Car Culture and 2024 ZAMAC variations. Looking at the STH item for this case, this sure is an all-American party.
Super Treasure Hunt Photo: eBay/user ck_salez Speaking of which, the ‘87 Dodge D100 is the second American car in the STH line for 2027. The ‘64 Lincoln Continental came first and we know a ‘67 Shelby GT500 is also on its way.
We’ve already seen more than half of the STH collectibles for next year, and the Dodge is the only pickup truck thus far. We had the ‘23 Ram 1500 in that “category” this year, the 2020 Jeep Gladiator and 1975 Datsun Sunny Truck in 2025, and you’ll find two more of them in 2024.
Brendon Vetuskey created the D100 back in 2018, and I remember finding its Treasure Hunt variation in 2022. It’s not often that a Hot Wheels casting shows up in both series.
I can remember seeing certain cars with two TH or two STH iterations though. I’ve already spotted the Dodge listed for as much as $140 on eBay, and I don’t believe it can go higher up than that.
Case D Highlights Photo: Done Teka I’m sure the El Segundo-based manufacturer still has plenty of surprises in store for 2027, despite all the sneak peak previews and the leaked photos and pre-order information. If you don’t typically pay attention to those you might have even more fun throughout the year. Some might even call it delayed gratification. I knew the Tyco Turbo Hopper was on its way, but wasn’t sure which case it would be part of.
Mattel’s strategy of recreating old, iconic toys is fairly impressive and will probably render good results in the long run. While I have never played with the original version of this machine before, I’m excited about the new suspension setup as it’s not something we can typically enjoy in the Hot Wheels universe. Thomas Kim has only created four castings so far, and the Starting Bloc is one of them.
It’s the result of imagining what a Can Am racer would have looked like if it used wood instead of conventional materials. It looks fun but I don’t think I’ll ever buy one. For a moment, I was almost certain the ‘70 Buick GSX was part of Case C. Then I realized it just has the same livery as the ‘87 Buick Regal GNX, something we’ve seen with other vehicles before.
It’s a fun way to highlight how cars have changed over the years, especially in the Then and Now mini-series. Cool-One has been around for over 20 years now, as Mark Jones created it for the 2004 First Editions collection. It’s not an item I’ve ever played with, though, although I vaguely remember an Art Cars version of it from 2017. The Brain Freeze livery is interesting, but I’d still go after a more traditional ice cream van.
Photo: Done Teka To me, one of the most exciting cars inside Case D has got to be the Porsche 934 Turbo RSR. I remember collecting all the variations I could find since its debut in 2014. It has evaded me for a few years now, although I am partly responsible for that as I didn’t enjoy the Neon Speeders release. Next year will be its first time back in the Mainline collection since 2019! And it’s using the same Lace Wire wheels it has in the Exotics mini-collection back then.
Fast Gassin has been MIA for a few years now, with no new variations since the 2023 HW Circle Track 5-Pack release. The 2027 version looks a lot like the casting’s First Edition from 2009, although that had two extra wheels to show off. The Chevy Silverado Off Road is starting to show its age, and it just isn’t the same without the Real Riders wheels.
At least it has new rims on, which is a plus. I’ve seen so many previews of the Draguar already that the only thing I care about is having it home for an unboxing session. It might be too soon to hope other castings will feature the opening body in this entry-level series though. The sixth variation of Vetuskey’s K.I.T.T. Super Pursuit Mode is coming right up after a four year hiatus. As far as I can tell, it’s identical to 2022’s Mainline debut iteration.
I still haven’ seen the show yet, so there’s no incentive for me to get one for my collection. The Radford Type 62-2 Pikes Peak isn’t available in the Mattel Creations Elite 64 shop anymore, and I’m sorry I didn’t get it when I had the chance. That doesn’t automatically mean the new Type 62-2 Roadster will simply fly off the pegs, even though it has brand new wheels on. They’re 4-spokes but remind of the Star 5-Spoke design from the Silver Series.
Photo: Done Teka Is it just me or does the Fiat Beast of Turin look even better in black than it did in red? There’s even a ZAMAC version on the market, which makes the Throwback Cruisers model the fourth one so far. The Custom 2020 Honda e is new to the case and I simply cannot imagine it will ever feel like a classic, the way the ‘90s EG and EK models feel today. The Dodge Coronet Superbee could have easily been the Treasure Hunt collectible for Case D, as the Stingassic Six livery is bound to make it highly desirable.
I’m sure anyone who’s a fan of Brendon Vetuskey’s work will think the same. I have mixed feelings about the new ‘09 Corvette ZR1 even though yellow is my favorite color for it. It spent several years as a Multipack Exclusive between 2017 and 2019, and then vanished without a trace. I’m adding its first three iterations from 2008 on my “Must-have” list as we speak. You’ll spot a few more interesting items in the photo gallery, so consider the rest of the list a “surprise” as to what’s inside Case D!

This Mercedes C-Class Costs a Lot Less Than America’s Cheapest New Car
18 photos
Photo: Instagram | phoenix_motor_collection
While we usually focus on either high-end vehicles or those that rock serious firepower when it comes to our “ used car ” section, we decided to make an exception this time, as the ride you see in the gallery below does not boast a neck-snapping amount of power, and it also does not cost an arm and a leg.
Far from it, actually, as there are some people out there who paid more for an electric bicycle. And we are still talking about a modern premium compact sports sedan, which rocks a cool specification, this writer thinks, and boasts plenty of equipment. And if you lack the cash to buy it, then fret not, because the selling dealer offers financing.
More on that and on the Benjamins in a few moments, as first we have to tell you that you are looking at a Mercedes-Benz C-Class from the 2019 model year. This makes it part of the fourth-generation. The W205 was manufactured between 2014 and 2021, and besides the four-door sedan, it was also offered as a station wagon, as well as a coupe and a cabriolet. This was the model’s last generation available with a two-door body style, as these variants were replaced by the first-ever CLE starting with the next generation.
Assembly took place at several factories worldwide, including in Germany, at the Bremen facility, and in the United States, at the Tuscaloosa factory in Alabama. The fourth-gen Mercedes C-Class was also put together in Brazil, South Africa, India, China, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Thailand. The powertrain family varied from one region to another, and included several gasoline engines, a few diesels, and even hybrid power.
Photo: Instagram | phoenix_motor_collection Pictured above is a Mercedes-Benz C 300. This means that it packs a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine, which developed 242 hp (245 ps/180 kW) and 270 lb-ft (370 Nm) of torque when the car was new. This was pretty much a mid-range version of the car, power-wise, as superior variants included the 400 4Matic, 450 4Matic, C 43, C 63, and C 63 S. The C 250, C 200, C 180, and C 160 sat at the lower part of the lineup when it came to the gasoline powertrain lineup.
This ride features a glossy black look, rides on black and chrome wheels, features some chrome accents on the outside, and tinted windows. It has a black leather interior, sports a sunroof, ambient lighting, heated and ventilated seats, Bluetooth and Apple CarPlay connectivity, air conditioning, a reversing camera, blind spot monitoring, and other stuff. The selling dealer says that it has a clean title, and that it runs perfectly.
The asking price at the time of writing was $16,900, and as we already told you, this makes it more affordable than America’s cheapest new car , the Hyundai Venue, which has an MSRP of $20,850 for the 2027 model year in the entry-level grade called the SE. All-New Bentley Flying Spur Goes British Racing Green With Round Headlights in Fresh Renderings
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The ultra-luxury British automaker Bentley is focused solely on its first all-electric nameplate, Torcal, a crossover SUV packing up to 876 hp on the dedicated PPE architecture shared with the recent Porsche Cayenne Electric.
The latest model was launched not long ago, in September 2026, sharing the Premium Platform Electric (PPE) with the mighty Porsche, but it has already received a special commission, dubbed Bentley x FRGMT Torcal , which is a fashion-inspired collaboration in 20 units with Hiroshi Fujiwara, “a pioneer of Tokyo’s Ura-Harajuku streetwear movement.”
Of course, not everyone around the world needs or wants a zero-emission Bentley. The company still offers the ICE and hybrid Bentayga, Continental GT, and Flying Spur models, plus the limited Supersports, thus offering ample choice. But that doesn’t mean the new EV model, which introduces a fresh design language for the automaker, won’t influence the future of the other models in the lineup.
At least that’s the opinion across the rumor mill and the parallel universes of vehicular CGI where the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators usually dwell around. For example, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on a new Bentley – all over again.
Initially, the pixel master created an unofficial, hypothetical design project focused on the potential all-new fourth-gen (modern) Bentley Flying Spur or a massive refresh of the current third generation for the good folks over at Kolesa . The new sedan was heavily influenced by the styling of the Torcal, both at the front and around the back.
Alas, that didn’t bode well for the CGI expert, who had other plans for Bentley – he returned for a comprehensive digital transformation of the ultra-luxury sedan, this time around in a vibrant crimson hue and only keeping the Torcal-influenced styling around the rear, where it’s less damaging. At the front, on the other hand, the author actually went back in time, and the new Flying Spur has returned to classic double round LED headlights, this time with LED daytime halo rings and the new style of grille as on the Torcal.
But wait, there was more – together with Kolesa, the virtual artist also thought about a refreshed or all-new Bentley Continental GT, and this time around the news outlet also thought the double round headlight idea was better than the one they had initially with the Flying Spur. And it was also dressed in another vibrant hue – this time a metallic orange shade .
Nope, we’re not done yet. Just recently, the pixel master has again refocused their attention on the Bentley Flying Spur – now dressed in classic British Racing Green attire and taken out of the studio against a rainy British backdrop. There’s even a comparison with the Rolls-Royce Ghost, too! View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)
